tweets.title: @abeirami I will reiterate my earlier comment. As a reviewer, you voluntarily agree to do a service to the scientific community and your peers, NOT a DISSERVICE
tweets.body: @abeirami I will reiterate my earlier comment. As a reviewer, you voluntarily agree to do a service to the scientific community and your peers, NOT a DISSERVICE.  While it’s voluntary and unpaid, it doesn’t give  you any rights to do a disservice.

tweets.title: @AnkaReuel @NeurIPSConf Comparable situation on my end, we just withdrew the paper. The only impression I got from @NeurIPSConf was that our paper was reviewed
tweets.body: @AnkaReuel @NeurIPSConf Comparable situation on my end, we just withdrew the paper. The only impression I got from @NeurIPSConf was that our paper was reviewed either by bachelor students or ppl who have a special ability to read only 1% of what is written. We got only 1 more or less reasonable review.

tweets.title: Honestly, I am baffled by the #NeurIPS2024 reviews. We should have some preventive measure in place discouraging overly confident unprofessional reviews. In my
tweets.body: Honestly, I am baffled by the #NeurIPS2024 reviews. We should have some preventive measure in place discouraging overly confident unprofessional reviews. In my case, all the reviewers are strongly confident in their “thoughtful” feedback and “deeply intelligent” questions.

tweets.title: @peter_richtarik At least you got reviewers who can distinguish between convex and non-convex settings. In nowadays reviewing process, that’s a huge achievement
tweets.body: @peter_richtarik At least you got reviewers who can distinguish between convex and non-convex settings. In nowadays reviewing process, that’s a huge achievement on its own. We recently got a reviewer who was struggling to understand the extent of improvement from a QPTAS to a PTAS.

tweets.title: @peter_richtarik If you agree and change the terminology, papers that will cite your paper will stick to the new terminology, consequently creating a duplicate
tweets.body: @peter_richtarik If you agree and change the terminology, papers that will cite your paper will stick to the new terminology, consequently creating a duplicate terminology for the same problem/algorithm, which is going to complicate the lit. review for authors who will be working on that topic.
